audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Smash is called a dash and a gap-close in eight strings — 'his empowered Q dashes onto you', 'blink over his empowered-Q gap-close', 'dodge his empowered-Q stun', 'blink away the instant he commits the dash'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Volibear gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks.' It is a movement-speed buff plus a stun on his next attack, not a dash — there is no leap to sidestep and no travel to blink over. The advice 'bait the dash then blink the instant he commits' describes a moment that never happens; what actually happens is he runs at you faster than you walk and the stun lands on an auto-attack. That makes it an auto-attack reset with a wind-up tell, which is the flagged interaction, and it makes Riftwalk the answer for the opposite reason the page gives: a blink beats a run-down precisely because there is nothing for him to follow. 12s at rank 1, 300 range.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash is a run-down, not a dash: he gains speed toward you and the stun lands on his next attack. Riftwalk beats it because a blink cannot be chased — the attack wind-up is your cue, not the cast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (Q description, cooldown 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, range 300, autoReset flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Frenzied Maul is described as a 'bite' that 'slows and heals him', with no mention of the two-cast condition — and it does not slow.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Volibear damages an enemy, applying on-hit effects and marking them. Casting this ability again on the same target deals bonus damage and Heals Volibear.' The heal only arrives on the SECOND cast into the same target, and the ability carries no slow flag at all. That is the whole counterplay and the page misses it: break the mark before the second bite and he gets damage without sustain, which is exactly what a 500-range blink is for. The invented slow also matters, because it is the stated reason the page tells you that you cannot kite him. 5s cooldown, 325 range.
audit.corrected: Frenzied Maul heals him only on the second cast into the same target, and it does not slow. Leave the mark before the follow-up bite and his sustain never happens.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (W description, cooldown 5, range 325, heal + onHit flags and no slow flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Stormbringer is called a shield ('his R shield', 'his R is up to shield the dive', 'R shield, size buff'), and its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Volibear leaps to a target location, Slowing and damaging enemies beneath him while gaining bonus Health. Enemy towers near his landing location become temporarily disabled.' Bonus health is not a shield — it does not decay, and anti-shield thinking sends you looking for a window that never opens. Two much more useful facts are absent instead. It is 160/135/110 seconds, by a distance the longest cooldown in the matchup and therefore the cleanest green light on the page. And it disables towers where he lands, which is the actual reason he can kill you under your own turret pre-6 — a thing the page never warns about at all.
audit.corrected: Stormbringer: 160s at rank 1, 550 range. It gives him bonus health, not a shield, and it disables your tower where he lands — that is how the pre-6 dive kills you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Volibear all seven stages, but whys[6] ends '— the 66.67% win rate is yours to close out', spikes[2] says 'you hit even', and spikes[3] says you blink-chain to burst him.
audit.why: The chart contradicts three of its own rows on the same card, and it contradicts them in the same direction. The page's considered reading is: level 6 is a survival pivot and still his (spikes[1] says so explicitly — 'even if the lane isn't yours yet'), the first item brings you level, and two items are yours. I moved only the last two cells, changed win[N] and phases[N].side together so the layers cannot disagree, and left levels 1 through 6 exactly as they were.
audit.corrected: First item is Skill at 5/10; two-plus items is Kassadin at 6/10. Levels 1-6 stay Volibear.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sky Splitter is not mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: It is his only ranged tool — 1200 units, 16 seconds — and Riot's text says it grants him a shield only 'if he's inside the blast radius'. Both halves matter. The 1200 range is how he touches you while you last-hit at the tip of Null Sphere, which the page presents as a safe activity. And the conditional shield is a read: if he throws Sky Splitter onto you from outside it he gets a slow and no shield, and that is the version of the trade you can take.
audit.corrected: Sky Splitter is 1200 range on 16s and only shields him if he stands in his own blast. Poked from range, he gets a slow and nothing else.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (E description, cooldown 16, range 1200, shield flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late: 'Q-silence the counterplay'. Also the _missing-interactions file claims Volibear 'can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Thundering Smash' — I did not write that in.
audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield; it has never silenced in this kit version. The your-channel-punished flag is itself a false positive: it fires because the kit builder tagged Null Sphere with a 'channel' flag, but that flag came from parsing the words 'interrupting channels' in Kassadin's own tooltip. Null Sphere is a point-and-click orb, not a channel, so there is nothing for Thundering Smash to cancel and writing that in would have introduced a new error.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence, and it is not itself a channel that his stun can cancel.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (Q description and its 'channel' derived flag)

audit.why: 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' is already in Itemization, covering the flagged needs-antiheal interaction on Frenzied Maul. Nothing to add.
66.67% over 6 games, and whys[6] quotes it correctly as 66.67%. Six games is a very thin sample, which is why the chart move above leans on the page's own prose rather than on this number.

edits.before: Volibear owns these levels and you have to respect it — his empowered Q (Thundering Smash) dashes onto you with a stun, and his W bite both slows you and heals him, so he wins every all-in while your Null Sphere is mana-starved and you have no escape. Do not trade autos: last-hit at the tip of your Q and hold Null Sphere's shield to absorb the burst the moment he dashes in. If he commits the W bite, you cannot brawl a champion who heals off you this early — eat one hit and walk, conceding CS over a fight you lose.
edits.after: Volibear owns these levels and you have to respect it — Thundering Smash (12s at rank 1) is a run-down, not a dash: he gains speed toward you and the stun lands on his next attack, so the wind-up is your cue. Frenzied Maul only heals him on the SECOND bite into the same target, which is the one thing you control here. Last-hit at the tip of your Q, hold the Null Sphere shield for the stun, and after the first bite walk out of the mark — conceding CS beats feeding his sustain.

edits.before: Nether Blade's quintupled mana restore on champion hits finally lets you sustain and farm under tower, and a maxed Q chips him, but you're still only stabilizing — this is weather-the-storm, not a fight window. Level 6 is the pivot: Riftwalk lets you blink over his empowered-Q gap-close and out of W-bite range, so the dives that killed you pre-6 now whiff. Bait the empowered Q by faking a step forward, then blink away the instant he commits the dash — once that engage is on cooldown he has no way to stick to you.
edits.after: Nether Blade's mana restore on champion hits finally lets you sustain and farm under tower, and a maxed Q chips him, but you're still only stabilizing — weather-the-storm, not a fight window. Level 6 is the pivot: Riftwalk beats a run-down precisely because there is nothing to chase, so blink out of Frenzied Maul's mark before the second bite and his heal never lands. Watch Stormbringer as well: 160s at rank 1, and it disables your tower where he lands, which is how the pre-6 dive kills you.

edits.before: This is the game you played for. With Rod of Ages stacked and Nashor's or Lich Bane online, your Void Stone's 15% magic reduction does little against his physical brawl, but you don't need to tank him — you blink-chain Riftwalk and delete his carries while he flails. He's far too immobile to catch a stacking Riftwalk, and his W heal can't keep up with your burst-and-reposition. Just don't get greedy into his empowered-Q range while his R is up to shield the dive and buff his size.
edits.after: This is the game you played for. With Rod of Ages stacked and Nashor's or Lich Bane online, Void Stone bites into his passive's magic chain damage but little else — you don't need to tank him anyway, you blink-chain Riftwalk and delete his carries while he flails. He's far too immobile to catch a stacking Riftwalk, and Frenzied Maul needs a second bite on the same target to heal at all. Just don't get greedy while Stormbringer is up to add bonus health and disable a tower.

edits.after: Riftwalk beats a run-down stun outright, and it takes you out of the Frenzied Maul mark before his healing second bite lands.

notes: The _missing-interactions entry 'Volibear can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Thundering Smash (Q) — only channel once their CC is spent' is a FALSE POSITIVE and I did not write it in. It fires off the 'channel' derived flag on Kassadin's Null Sphere, but that flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact of the phrase 'interrupting channels' in Kassadin's own description — Null Sphere is a point-and-click orb, not a channel. Every 'your-channel-punished' row generated for Kassadin in that file will be wrong for the same reason (Warwick has one too), so the rule needs the flag source excluded rather than the individual rows edited. Sky Splitter is absent from the page entirely; I documented it in the audit but did not force it into a string, since the only places it would fit are already carrying higher-value corrections and the length band leaves no room.
